Hi Emily — thanks again for taking time today. Quick follow-up from our discovery so we can map the simplest commercial path for your pilot. Notes below (TL;DR and asks at the top):

TL;DR — we can support both PO and card. To finalize, we need: (1) your AP policy threshold for card purchases, (2) a PO contact/person who can issue a PO if needed, and (3) confirmation whether you want to buy via AWS Marketplace (faster procurement) or direct contract.

Call highlights:
- Pilot scope: 10k tokens/month; 1 dedicated dev seat for integration; 2-week evaluation window.
- Security: SOC2 in place, customer-managed VPC option requested for prod.
- Procurement signal: procurement team prefers formal PO for vendor spend > $5k/month; smaller purchases can be done on company card.

Open questions / asks (please reply inline):
1) AP threshold for card purchases (what spend triggers PO?) — we need the numeric limit.
2) PO routing: do you have a vendor ID and a standard PO template? If so, can you share the contact who issues POs?
3) Marketplace: would you prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace (Redwood listing) or direct invoicing? Marketplace reduces procurement friction but uses card or consolidated invoicing depending on your org.
4) Contract term: interested in a 3-month pilot then monthly rolling? Any procurement guardrails around auto-renewals?

Attached: draft SOW with pilot deliverables and a pricing sheet for the pilot. I marked the invoice cadence options (monthly vs net 30 on PO).

Next steps I propose (pending your answers):
- If AP requires PO: we’ll prepare a brief PO-ready invoice and routing guide and loop our finance.
- If card: we’ll enable a short-term card charge for the pilot and recontract if you expand.
- If marketplace: we’ll send a Marketplace procurement note and a checklist for your vendor team.

Thanks — if easier, loop in your AP contact and drop their email and I’ll send the PO-ready docs directly.

Best,
Priya

Thanks Priya — good recap and appreciate the SOW. Answering inline: 

> 1) AP threshold for card purchases (what spend triggers PO?)
We have a $4,000 monthly card threshold for ad-hoc purchases. Anything above that needs a PO. For recurring subscriptions classified as "vendor services" our AP team prefers a PO regardless if it exceeds $1,000/month, but they do make exceptions for pilots under $5k total. Confusing, I know.

> 2) PO routing: do you have a vendor ID and a standard PO template? If so, can you share the contact who issues POs?
I'll try to get our vendor ID and the PO template. The person who issues POs is "Lena Hoffman" in AP (ap@albatrossbio.com). I'm CC'ing AP so they see the thread.

> 3) Marketplace: would you prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace or direct invoicing?
We'd prefer Marketplace only if it can be invoiced to our central cloud chargeback center. If Marketplace forces us to use a card and we exceed the threshold, it creates extra work. So Marketplace is OK only if AP confirms consolidated invoicing.

> 4) Contract term: any procurement guardrails around auto-renewals?
AP does not allow auto-renewals unless there is a business justification and the budget owner signs off. For a pilot, they prefer month-to-month or an explicit opt-in to renew.

Looping Lena for AP context. Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up tomorrow morning if helpful.

—Emily
Emily Park
Head of Data Science, Albatross Bio
